questions.topic: Changes In Half-Cell After One Hour
questions.question: Explain the changes that would occur in the right-hand half-cell when the voltmeter is removed and the cell runs for one hour.
questions.answer: The changes in the right-hand half-cell depend on which half-cell is right-hand electrode system 8 in the Data Booklet, and the booklet page is not in the paper.

questions.question: Explain, by calculating E-zero values, why Fe(II) reduces Cr(VI) to Cr(III) but zinc is needed to reduce Cr(VI) to Cr(II). (Data Booklet values needed.)
questions.answer: Fe2+ (Fe3+/Fe2+ = +0.77 V) reduces Cr2O7 2- (+1.33 V) to Cr3+ with E-zero(cell) = +0.56 V but cannot reduce Cr3+ to Cr2+ (-0.41 V, E-zero(cell) = -1.18 V); Zn (Zn2+/Zn = -0.76 V) can, E-zero(cell) = +0.35 V.
steps: Data Booklet values: Cr2O7 2- + 14H+ + 6e- <=> 2Cr3+ + 7H2O is +1.33 V; Cr3+ + e- <=> Cr2+ is -0.41 V; Fe3+ + e- <=> Fe2+ is +0.77 V; Zn2+ + 2e- <=> Zn is -0.76 V.
Fe(II) with Cr(VI): E-zero(cell) = +1.33 - (+0.77) = +0.56 V, positive, so Fe2+ reduces Cr(VI) to Cr(III).
Fe(II) with Cr(III): E-zero(cell) = -0.41 - (+0.77) = -1.18 V, negative, so Fe2+ cannot reduce Cr(III) to Cr(II) and the reduction stops at Cr(III).
Zinc with Cr(III): E-zero(cell) = -0.41 - (-0.76) = +0.35 V, positive, so zinc is a strong enough reducing agent to take Cr(III) on to Cr(II).

questions.question: State the essential condition required for these reactions to occur.
questions.answer: Acidic conditions (a source of H+ ions).
steps: Reduction of Cr(VI) uses H+ in the half-equations.
So the reactions need an acidic solution.

questions.question: What are the electronic structures of the three copper species in the reaction sequence? (Sequence diagram needed.)
questions.answer: D: Cu [Ar] 3d10 4s1, Cu+ [Ar] 3d10, Cu2+ [Ar] 3d9
steps: Copper is an exception to the filling order: the atom is [Ar] 3d10 4s1 so that the 3d subshell is full.
Cu+ loses the 4s electron, giving [Ar] 3d10; Cu2+ loses one 3d electron as well, giving [Ar] 3d9.
This matches row D.

keywords: P Q R S T U
questions.question: Which rows show the substances with their correct oxidation states? (Table needed.)
questions.answer: C: Cu(0) = T, Cu(I) = S, Cu(II) = P
steps: T is the pink solid, which is copper metal, Cu(0).
S is the colourless solution from CuI plus ammonia, [Cu(NH3)2]+, which contains Cu(I).
P is the blue copper(II) solution (also Q, R and U are Cu(II)), so the row is T, S, P, option C.

questions.question: Aqueous solution X contains copper species. Which of A H2SO4, B KI, C NaOH, D NH3 is it? (Sequence diagram needed.)
questions.answer: D: NH3
steps: X turns pale blue Q (Cu(OH)2) into a dark blue solution R, which is [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+.
X also turns CuI into a colourless solution S, which is [Cu(NH3)2]+.
Both are ammine complexes, so X is aqueous ammonia, NH3.

questions.question: Explain why the [Fe(H2O)6]2+ complex ion is coloured.
questions.answer: The d orbitals are split by the water ligands; an electron absorbs visible light to move between split d levels, so the complex is coloured.
steps: Fe2+ is 3d6 with partly filled d orbitals.
Water ligands split the d orbitals into two energy levels.
An electron absorbs visible light to move from the lower to the higher level (d-d transition).
The colour seen is the complementary colour of the absorbed light, here green.

questions.question: Explain why [Fe(H2O)6]2+ and [Fe(H2O)6]3+ are different colours.
questions.answer: Fe2+ is 3d6 and Fe3+ is 3d5, and the higher charge of Fe3+ changes the d-level energy gap, so different wavelengths are absorbed.
steps: Fe2+ has 3d6 and Fe3+ has 3d5, so they have different numbers of d electrons.
The higher charge on Fe3+ increases the splitting of the d orbitals.
So they absorb different wavelengths and show different colours.

questions.question: Complete the alternative dot-and-cross diagram of the thiocyanate ion with the negative charge on sulfur. (Diagram needed.)
questions.answer: Draw S-C with one shared pair and C-N with three shared pairs (a triple bond); S has three lone pairs (five * plus the extra electron, shown as the triangle) and N has one lone pair, giving S(-)-C#N.
steps: The ion is drawn as S(-)-C#N, with 8 outer electrons on each atom.
Between S and C put one shared pair: one * and one x.
Between C and N put three shared pairs: three x and three dots.
Around S put three lone pairs: five * plus the triangle (the extra electron) making six electrons, and the negative sign on S; around N put one lone pair of two dots.

questions.question: 12.8 cm3 of 0.05 mol dm-3 FeCl3 reacts with 8.0 cm3 of 0.08 mol dm-3 NH4SCN. Deduce the formula of the octahedral complex ion formed in aqueous solution.
questions.answer: [Fe(H2O)5(SCN)]2+
steps: Ratio Fe3+ : SCN- = 1 : 1, so one SCN- ligand per Fe3+.
The octahedral complex has six ligands; the other five are water.
Formula: [Fe(H2O)5(SCN)]2+.

questions.question: Plot a graph of absorbance against concentration using the data table for copper(II) sulfate at 635 nm. (Data table not in text.)
questions.answer: Plot concentration on the x-axis (0 to 0.50 mol dm-3) and absorbance on the y-axis (0 to 1.40), with labelled axes and units; the points lie on a straight line through the origin with gradient about 2.76 dm3 mol-1.
steps: Use a scale that fills more than half of the grid: x-axis concentration of CuSO4 / mol dm-3, y-axis absorbance at 635 nm.
Draw a single straight best-fit line through the origin and the points; absorbance is directly proportional to concentration (about 2.76 x concentration).

questions.question: 50.0 cm3 of unknown CuSO4 diluted to 250.0 cm3 has absorbance 0.72 at 635 nm. Use the graph to determine the original concentration. (Graph needed.)
questions.answer: Original concentration = 1.3 mol dm-3
steps: From the calibration line (absorbance = 2.76 x concentration), an absorbance of 0.72 corresponds to a concentration of 0.72 / 2.76 = 0.26 mol dm-3; show the horizontal line from 0.72 to the graph then down to the axis.
The 50.0 cm3 was diluted to 250.0 cm3, a dilution factor of 5.
Original concentration = 0.26 x 5 = 1.3 mol dm-3.

questions.question: Give one reason why concentrations above 0.50 mol dm-3 read from the graph are uncertain.
questions.answer: At high concentration the absorbance is no longer proportional to concentration (the graph is non-linear), so readings are uncertain.
steps: The calibration relationship holds only over a linear range.
At high concentration the absorbance levels off, so the line is no longer straight.
So values read from it above 0.50 mol dm-3 are less reliable.

questions.question: Give a reason, referring to the equation, why formation of the diamine complex from the aqueous complex ion is thermodynamically favoured.
questions.answer: The number of particles increases (4 to 7), giving a positive entropy change that favours the reaction.
steps: Left: [Co(H2O)6]3+ plus 3 en = 4 species.
Right: [Co(en)3]3+ plus 6 H2O = 7 species.
More particles gives a positive entropy change, so the reaction is favoured.

questions.question: Explain, by reference to its structure, why ethane-1,2-diamine is a bidentate ligand.
questions.answer: It has two nitrogen atoms, each with a lone pair, so it forms two dative covalent bonds to the metal.
steps: Ethane-1,2-diamine is H2N-CH2-CH2-NH2.
Each NH2 group has a lone pair on N that can be donated.
Two donor atoms bond to the same metal ion, so the ligand is bidentate.

questions.question: Explain how the H-N-H bond angles in ethane-1,2-diamine change when the complex ion forms.
questions.answer: The H-N-H bond angles increase slightly (from about 107 towards 109.5 degrees) because the N lone pair becomes a bonding pair, reducing lone pair repulsion.
steps: In free ethane-1,2-diamine, each N has a lone pair, which repels bonding pairs more strongly.
On complex formation the lone pair is donated to Co3+, forming a bonding pair to Co.
Lone pair repulsion is reduced, so the H-N-H bond angle increases towards 109.5 degrees.

questions.question: What colour is vanadium(III) in aqueous solution? A blue, B green, C purple, D yellow.
questions.answer: B - green
steps: V3+ in aqueous solution is [V(H2O)6]3+, which is green.
So the answer is B.

questions.question: Which pair of equations shows the most likely mechanism for V2O5 acting as a catalyst in the contact process? (Options not in text.)
questions.answer: D: V2O5 + SO2 -> V2O4 + SO3, then V2O4 + 1/2 O2 -> V2O5
steps: The catalyst is used in one step and regenerated in the next, with V2O5 oxidising SO2 to SO3.
Step 1: V2O5 oxidises SO2 to SO3 and is reduced from V(+5) to V2O4 (V(+4)).
Step 2: O2 reoxidises V2O4 back to V2O5, so the catalyst is unchanged.
Option D is the only pair that is balanced and regenerates V2O5 with sensible vanadium oxidation states.

questions.question: Which graph shows the autocatalysis of the reaction between manganate(VII) and ethanedioate by manganese(II) ions? (Graph options not in text.)
questions.answer: D: an S-shaped curve (slow start, steeper middle, then levelling off)
steps: Mn2+ is a product that catalyses the reaction (autocatalysis), so the rate starts slow and increases as Mn2+ forms.
CO2 is produced slowly at first, then faster, giving an increasing gradient.
When the reactants run out the volume of CO2 reaches a maximum and the curve levels off, giving an S-shape (graph D).
C has an increasing gradient but never levels off, so it is not a complete reaction; A is a constant rate; B is a normal rate that starts fastest.

questions.question: Chromium(III) hydroxide is amphoteric. It dissolves in: A water, B strong acid only, C strong alkali only, D strong acid and strong alkali.
questions.answer: D - strong acid and strong alkali
steps: An amphoteric hydroxide reacts with both acids and bases.
Cr(OH)3 dissolves in acid to form [Cr(H2O)6]3+ and in alkali to form [Cr(OH)6]3-.
So the answer is D.

questions.question: Which successive ionisation energies are most likely to be those of a transition element? (Options not in text.)
steps: Transition elements have 4s and 3d electrons of similar energy, so the successive ionisation energies rise gradually.
Row B shows a steady rise with no huge jump, so it is a d-block element (it matches iron).
A has a huge jump after the third value (group 3, Al), C after the fourth (group 4, Si) and D after the third (group 3, B), so none of these is a transition element.

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of a chromium atom? A [Ar] 3d4 4s2, B [Ar] 3d5 4s1, C [Ar] 3d6, D [Ar] 3d1 4s2 4p3.
questions.answer: B - [Ar] 3d5 4s1
steps: Cr is an exception to the aufbau order.
One 4s electron moves to 3d to give a half-filled 3d5 subshell.
So Cr is [Ar] 3d5 4s1.

questions.question: What is the best explanation for the high activation energy of the peroxodisulfate and iodide reaction? A peroxodisulfate is a weak oxidising agent, B iodide is a weak reducing agent, C both ions are negatively charged, D three reactant ions are involved.
questions.answer: C - peroxodisulfate and iodide ions are both negatively charged
steps: Both reacting ions are negative, so they repel each other.
This repulsion means the collision needs more energy to overcome, raising Ea.
Options A and B are wrong since both are good oxidant and reductant.

questions.question: Which property of iron(II) ions lets them act as a catalyst for this reaction? A easily reduced to iron metal, B adsorb reactants, C easily oxidised and then reduced, D easily reduced and then oxidised.
questions.answer: C - iron(II) ions can be easily oxidised and then reduced
steps: Fe2+ is oxidised to Fe3+ by peroxodisulfate.
Fe3+ is reduced back to Fe2+ by iodide.
So the catalyst is oxidised then reduced: option C.

questions.question: Which ion shows the typical property of transition metals by forming coloured complexes? A Cu+, B Ni2+, C Sc3+, D Zn2+.
questions.answer: B - Ni2+
steps: Ni2+ is 3d8 (partly filled), so it forms coloured complexes.
Cu+ (3d10), Sc3+ (3d0) and Zn2+ (3d10) have no partly filled d subshell, so they are colourless.

questions.question: Explain why the three hydration isomers of chromium(III) chloride have different colours.
questions.answer: Different numbers of Cl- and H2O ligands give different ligand field splitting, so each isomer absorbs a different wavelength and has a different colour.
steps: The three isomers have different ligands around Cr3+ (H2O and Cl- in different numbers).
Cl- and H2O produce different d-orbital splitting energies.
Different splitting means different wavelengths are absorbed by d-d transitions.
So each isomer shows a different colour.

questions.question: Suggest how to determine quantitatively the relative numbers of free chloride ions in three equimolar solutions of the isomers using the standard chloride test.
questions.answer: Add excess silver nitrate to equal volumes of each solution, filter, dry and weigh the AgCl precipitate, and compare masses.
steps: Take equal volumes of the equimolar isomer solutions.
Add excess AgNO3(aq) to each so all free Cl- precipitates as AgCl.
Filter, wash and dry each precipitate in a weighed filter paper.
Weigh each AgCl precipitate; more AgCl means more free Cl-.
Compare the masses to find the relative numbers of free chloride ions.

questions.question: Write the balanced equation for Step 1, slow substitution of one chloride ligand by water in cisplatin.
questions.answer: PtCl2(NH3)2 + H2O -> [PtCl(NH3)2(H2O)]+ + Cl-
steps: One Cl- ligand is replaced by one H2O ligand.
The complex becomes [PtCl(NH3)2(H2O)]+ with one Cl- released.
Balance: PtCl2(NH3)2 + H2O -> [PtCl(NH3)2(H2O)]+ + Cl-.

questions.question: Describe how guanine and adenine bind to the platinum ion.
questions.answer: Through lone pairs on nitrogen atoms, which form dative covalent bonds to Pt2+ (monodentate ligands).
steps: Guanine and adenine each have a nitrogen atom with a lone pair.
This nitrogen donates the lone pair to Pt2+, forming a dative covalent bond.

questions.topic: Why Trans-Platin Does Not Damage DNA
questions.question: Suggest why trans-platin binds to DNA but does not damage it.
questions.answer: The two leaving groups are trans, so the platinum cannot bridge two bases and form a cross-link; it binds only one base on the strand.
steps: Cis-platin cross-links two bases because its two leaving groups are next to each other.
In trans-platin the two sites are on opposite sides, so they are too far apart to bridge two bases.
So trans-platin cannot form the cross-link that stops DNA replication.

questions.question: Reinecke's salt NH4[Cr(SCN)x(NH3)y].zH2O contains 14.67% Cr, 36.23% S, 4.51% O, 27.65% N. Calculate x, y and z.
steps: Thus x = 4 (S atoms from SCN-), and z = 1 (O from one water).
N total = 7 = 1 (NH4+) + 4 (SCN-) + y, so y = 2 (NH3 ligands).

questions.question: Draw a diagram of the anion of Reinecke's salt showing its three-dimensional shape.
questions.answer: An octahedral anion with Cr at the centre: two NH3 ligands trans (top and bottom, 180 degrees apart) and four SCN- ligands in the square plane at 90 degrees, bonded to Cr by dative bonds, with an overall charge of 1-.
steps: The anion is [Cr(SCN)4(NH3)2]-, which has six ligands, so it is octahedral with all bond angles 90 degrees.
It is the trans isomer, so the two NH3 ligands sit opposite each other along the vertical axis (180 degrees apart).
The four SCN- ligands lie in the horizontal plane around Cr (drawn with wedges and dashes for 3-D, bonded through N as in Reinecke's salt); put brackets and the 1- charge on the whole ion.

questions.question: Explain why the tetrahedral complex [Co(NH3)ClBrI] exists as two optical isomers.
questions.answer: It has four different ligands around the central Co atom, so it has no plane of symmetry and its two mirror images are non-superimposable.
steps: The four ligands NH3, Cl-, Br- and I- are all different.
A tetrahedral complex with four different ligands is chiral.
Its mirror images cannot be superimposed, so there are two optical isomers.

questions.question: Complete the diagram showing the two optical isomers of the tetrahedral complex [Co(NH3)ClBrI].
questions.answer: Label the four bonds of the left Co with NH3, Cl, Br and I (one each); draw the right-hand isomer as its mirror image, with the same four ligands but reflected so the two shapes cannot be superimposed.
steps: Left isomer: put NH3 on the upward bond, Cl on the lower-left plain bond, I on the hashed (backward) bond and Br on the wedge (forward) bond.

Right isomer: draw the reflection in a vertical mirror plane between the two: NH3 on the upward bond, Cl on the lower-right plain bond, I on the hashed bond going to the left and Br on the wedge going to the lower left.
The two are non-superimposable mirror images, so they are a pair of optical isomers (enantiomers).

questions.question: Complete the equation for the reaction of a laboratory reagent with aqueous Fe3+ to produce a precipitate, with state symbols.
questions.answer: Fe3+(aq) + 3OH-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s)
steps: The laboratory reagent is aqueous NaOH (or another alkali).
Fe3+ forms an insoluble hydroxide precipitate.
Balance: Fe3+(aq) + 3OH-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s).

questions.question: Complete the table for the nickel dithiocarbamate complex. (Table not in text.)
questions.answer: Charge on nickel ion: +2; type of ligand: bidentate; coordination number: 6; shape: octahedral
steps: The complex ion has overall charge 1- and contains three dithiocarbamate ligands, each 1-, so Ni = -1 - (3 x -1) = +2.
Each ligand binds through its two sulfur atoms (each with a lone pair), so it is bidentate.
Three bidentate ligands give 3 x 2 = 6 dative bonds, so the coordination number is 6 and the shape is octahedral.

questions.question: Explain, using a balanced equation, why forming the dithiocarbamate complex from aqueous nickel ions is thermodynamically feasible.
questions.answer: [Ni(H2O)6]2+ + 3(CH3)2NCS2- -> [Ni((CH3)2NCS2)3]- + 6H2O; the number of particles rises from 4 to 7, so entropy increases and the reaction is feasible.
steps: Write the equation: [Ni(H2O)6]2+ + 3(CH3)2NCS2- -> [Ni((CH3)2NCS2)3]- + 6H2O.
Left side 4 species, right side 7 species, so there are more particles on the right.
The entropy of the system increases (chelate effect), while the enthalpy change is small because six Ni-O dative bonds are replaced by six Ni-S dative bonds.
So Delta G = Delta H - T Delta S is negative and the formation of the complex is thermodynamically feasible.

questions.question: A 5 dm3 wastewater sample gives 245.0 mg of dry H+[Ni((CH3)2NCS2)3]- precipitate. Calculate the Ni2+ concentration in mol dm-3 (dithiocarbamate ion Mr 120.2).
steps: Moles precipitate = 0.2450 / 420.3 = 5.83 x 10^-4 mol.
Each precipitate has one Ni, so moles Ni2+ = 5.83 x 10^-4 mol.
Concentration = 5.83 x 10^-4 / 5 = 1.17 x 10^-4 mol dm-3.

questions.question: Which pair of elements are both transition metals? A gold and scandium, B gold and titanium, C scandium and zinc, D titanium and zinc.
questions.answer: B - gold and titanium
steps: Au and Ti are d-block elements that form ions with partly filled d subshells.
Sc3+ is 3d0 and Zn2+ is 3d10, so scandium and zinc are not transition elements in the strict sense.
So option B is correct.

questions.topic: Shapes Of Copper And Platinum Complexes
questions.question: What are the shapes of [CuCl4]2- and Pt(NH3)2Cl2? (Options not in text.)
questions.answer: C: [CuCl4]2- is tetrahedral and Pt(NH3)2Cl2 is square planar
steps: [CuCl4]2- has four large Cl- ligands around Cu2+, so it is tetrahedral.
Platinum(II) four-coordinate complexes such as Pt(NH3)2Cl2 are square planar.
This is option C.

questions.question: Which species cannot act as a ligand? A C2H6, B CO, C OH-, D C4H9NH2.
questions.answer: A - C2H6
steps: A ligand needs a lone pair to donate.
Ethane (C2H6) has no lone pairs (only C-C and C-H bonds).
CO, OH- and C4H9NH2 each have a lone pair.

questions.question: Complete the electronic configuration for the Fe2+ ion, given the configuration of Fe.
questions.answer: [Ar] 3d6
steps: Fe is [Ar] 3d6 4s2.
Fe2+ loses the two 4s electrons first.
So Fe2+ is [Ar] 3d6.

questions.question: Explain why an aqueous iron(II) sulfate solution, pale green, turns brown when left exposed to air, referring to the 3d configuration.
questions.answer: Fe2+ (3d6) is oxidised by O2 in air to Fe3+ (3d5), which is more stable, and the Fe3+ gives the brown colour.
steps: Fe2+ is 3d6, which can lose one electron to become 3d5.
Fe3+ (3d5, half-filled) is more stable than Fe2+ (3d6).
Dissolved oxygen oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+: 4Fe2+ + O2 + 4H+ -> 4Fe3+ + 2H2O.
Fe3+ solutions are yellow-brown, so the solution turns brown.

questions.question: 6.42 g moss killer made to 250 cm3; 25.0 cm3 titrated with 0.00740 mol dm-3 MnO4-, mean titre 17.70 cm3. Find the percentage by mass of FeSO4 (Mr 151.9).
questions.answer: 15.5% FeSO4 by mass

questions.question: Suggest why iron(II) sulfate is acidic when dissolved in water.
questions.answer: The small, highly charged Fe2+ ion polarises the O-H bonds of coordinated water, releasing H+ ions.
steps: [Fe(H2O)6]2+ is a small ion with a 2+ charge, so it has high charge density.
It polarises the O-H bonds of coordinated water, which releases H+: [Fe(H2O)6]2+ -> [Fe(H2O)5(OH)]+ + H+.
Releasing H+ makes the solution acidic.

questions.question: The first five ionisation energies of four elements are shown. Which are the ionisation energies of a transition metal? (Table not in text.)
steps: A transition metal shows a gradual rise in successive ionisation energies as the 4s and 3d electrons are removed, with no sudden large jump.
Row D rises steadily, so it is a transition metal (it is close to manganese).
A has a large jump after the 1st (group 1), B after the 3rd (Al, group 3) and C after the 2nd (Mg, group 2), so none of them is a transition metal.

questions.question: An aqueous transition metal ion absorbs light of green, yellow and red frequencies. Which ion is likely to be present? A Mn2+, B Co2+, C Ni2+, D Cu2+.
questions.answer: D - Cu2+ (blue solution, absorbs orange-red light)
steps: The solution transmits the complementary colour; absorbing green, yellow and red leaves blue/violet transmitted.
Cu2+(aq) is blue because it absorbs in the orange-red region.
Mn2+ is very pale pink, Co2+ is pink and Ni2+ is green, so they do not fit.

questions.question: What is the colour of the VO2+ ion in aqueous solution? Options: A blue, B green, C violet, D yellow. (The text does not show whether the ion is V(IV) or V(V).)
questions.answer: A: blue
steps: The ion is VO2+ with a 2+ charge (a superscript), which is the vanadyl ion containing vanadium(IV).
Aqueous vanadium(IV), VO2+, is blue; the yellow ion is VO2+ with charge 1+ (vanadium(V)), which is not the ion here.

questions.question: Write the equation for Reaction 1 in the chromium scheme using the half-equations from page 10 of the Data Booklet. (Reaction scheme not in text.)
steps: In Reaction 1 Cr3+ is oxidised to Cr2O7 2- by H2O2, which is reduced to water (H2O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> 2H2O, +1.77 V).
Oxidation: 2Cr3+ + 7H2O -> Cr2O7 2- + 14H+ + 6e-; reduction multiplied by 3: 3H2O2 + 6H+ + 6e- -> 6H2O.
Add and cancel water and H+: 2Cr3+ + 3H2O2 + H2O -> Cr2O7 2- + 8H+ (charge +6 on both sides).

questions.question: In Reaction 2, Cr2O7 2- reacts with metal M in acid to form Cr3+ and M2+. Identify a possible metal M using calculation. (Data Booklet needed.)
questions.answer: M = zinc: Cr2O7 2- + 14H+ + 3Zn -> 2Cr3+ + 3Zn2+ + 7H2O with E-zero(cell) = +1.33 - (-0.76) = +2.09 V (positive, so feasible)
steps: Reaction 2 is the reduction of Cr2O7 2- (+1.33 V) to Cr3+ by a metal that is oxidised to M2+, so M must have a more negative E-zero than +1.33 V.
Zinc (Zn2+/Zn = -0.76 V in the Data Booklet) is a suitable metal; iron (-0.44 V) would also work.
E-zero(cell) = +1.33 - (-0.76) = +2.09 V, which is positive.
Equation: Cr2O7 2- + 14H+ + 3Zn -> 2Cr3+ + 3Zn2+ + 7H2O.

questions.question: Give the formula of the species responsible for the purple colour in Reaction 3 and name the type of reaction. (Reaction scheme missing.)
questions.answer: [Cr(NH3)6]3+; a ligand substitution (ligand exchange) reaction
steps: In Reaction 3 excess aqueous ammonia is added to Cr3+(aq).
NH3 replaces the water ligands to give the purple hexaamminechromium(III) ion, [Cr(NH3)6]3+.
Ligands are swapped without changing the oxidation state, so this is ligand substitution (ligand exchange).

questions.question: State whether Reaction 4 is a redox reaction and justify using oxidation numbers. (Reaction scheme missing.)
questions.answer: Not a redox reaction: the oxidation number of chromium is +6 in both Cr2O7 2- and CrO4 2-, and that of O is -2 in both, so nothing is oxidised or reduced.
steps: Reaction 4 is Cr2O7 2- + 2OH- -> 2CrO4 2- + H2O (orange to yellow).
In Cr2O7 2- the chromium is +6; in CrO4 2- the chromium is also +6.
No oxidation number changes (O stays -2, H stays +1), so it is not redox; it is an acid-base reaction where OH- removes H+ from the equilibrium.

questions.question: Deduce the simplest formula of a double salt containing Cr3+, K+ and SO4 2-.
questions.answer: KCr(SO4)2
steps: Two SO4 2- (-4) balance the charge.
Formula: KCr(SO4)2.

questions.question: A hydrated double salt, after heating, keeps 56.74% of its original mass. Calculate the number of moles of water of crystallisation per mole of hydrated salt (anhydrous KCr(SO4)2 Mr = 283.3).
questions.answer: 12 moles of water (KCr(SO4)2.12H2O)
steps: Anhydrous mass fraction = 0.5674, so hydrated Mr = 283.3 / 0.5674 = 499.3.
Mass of water lost = 499.3 - 283.3 = 216.0.
Moles of water = 216.0 / 18.0 = 12.0.
So n = 12.

questions.question: Show by calculation that a blood sample with Cr3+ at 1.345 x 10^-7 mol dm-3 exceeds the safe limit of 4 ppb by mass (density 1.0 g cm-3).
questions.answer: About 7.0 ppb, which exceeds the 4 ppb limit.
steps: Mass of 1 dm3 of blood = 1.0 x 1000 = 1000 g (density 1.0 g cm-3).
6.99 ppb is greater than 4 ppb, so the limit is exceeded.

questions.question: Suggest how EDTA4- would treat Cr3+ poisoning, and why EDTA4- is preferred to 1,2-diaminoethane.
questions.answer: EDTA4- is hexadentate and forms a very stable chelate with Cr3+, removing it from the body; it is preferred because it forms a more stable complex than the bidentate en.
steps: EDTA4- binds Cr3+ through six donor atoms to form a stable chelate complex.
This complex is excreted, removing the toxic Cr3+ from the body.
EDTA4- is hexadentate, so it forms more bonds and a more stable complex than bidentate en (chelate effect).

questions.question: Which statement about a catalytic converter is not true? A the catalyst contains platinum, B CO and NO are absorbed by the catalyst, C desorption of CO2 and N2 takes place, D it is a heterogeneous reaction.
questions.answer: B - CO and NO are adsorbed (not absorbed) onto the catalyst surface
steps: Gases are adsorbed onto the surface of the catalyst, not absorbed into its bulk.
Platinum is used in catalytic converters, and the reaction is heterogeneous.
Products are desorbed from the surface after reaction.
So the false statement is B.

questions.question: Which is incorrect for H2O, OH- and NH3? A all can act as bidentate ligands, B all can act as electron pair donors, C all can form dative covalent bonds, D all can take part in complex ion formation.
questions.answer: A - all can act as bidentate ligands (they are monodentate)
steps: H2O, OH- and NH3 each have one lone pair to donate.
So each is monodentate, not bidentate.
Options B, C and D are all true.

questions.question: State the shape of the cis-platin complex PtCl2(NH3)2.
questions.answer: Square planar
steps: Pt2+ is d8 with four ligands (2 NH3, 2 Cl-).
Four-coordinate Pt(II) complexes are square planar.

questions.question: Draw the isomer trans-platin.
questions.answer: Square planar Pt with the two NH3 ligands opposite each other and the two Cl ligands opposite each other (trans).
steps: Place Pt at the centre of a square.
Put one NH3 and one Cl at adjacent corners, arranged so the two NH3 are on opposite sides.
Put the two Cl on the remaining opposite positions so each Cl is trans to a Cl and each NH3 is trans to an NH3.

questions.question: Suggest why, in human cells, the two chloride ions in cisplatin are replaced by water molecules.
questions.answer: Water is present in very high concentration in cells and is a neutral ligand, so it displaces chloride and the Cl- concentration in cells is low.
steps: Cells contain far more water (about 55 mol dm-3) than chloride ions.
The high concentration of water drives the ligand exchange by mass action.
Water is a good electron pair donor, so it can replace Cl- ligands.

questions.question: DNA acts as a ligand in the complex shown with cisplatin. Name this type of ligand.
questions.answer: Monodentate ligand (each DNA base donates one N lone pair)
steps: Each DNA base (guanine or adenine) donates one lone pair from a nitrogen atom.
Each dative bond comes from a separate donor atom, so each base is a monodentate ligand.

questions.question: Explain, by considering the equation PtCl2(NH3)2 + DNA -> [Pt(NH3)2(DNA)]2+ + 2Cl-, why this process is thermodynamically feasible.
questions.answer: The number of particles increases from 2 to 3, so entropy increases and the process is feasible.
steps: Left side: PtCl2(NH3)2 and DNA, 2 species.
Right side: [Pt(NH3)2(DNA)]2+ plus 2Cl-, 3 species.
Increase in particle number gives a positive entropy change, which makes the process feasible.

questions.question: What is the colour of an aqueous solution of V2+ ions? A blue, B green, C purple, D yellow.
questions.answer: C - purple (violet)
steps: V2+ is 3d3 and forms [V(H2O)6]2+.
Its d-d transitions absorb yellow-green light, so it appears violet/purple.

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of a Zn2+ ion? A [Ar] 3d10, B [Ar] 3d10 4s2, C [Ar] 3d9 4s1, D [Ar] 3d8 4s2.
questions.answer: A - [Ar] 3d10
steps: Zn is [Ar] 3d10 4s2.
Zn2+ loses the two 4s electrons.
So Zn2+ is [Ar] 3d10.

questions.question: Explain the changes when dilute aqueous ammonia is added gradually to [CuCl4]2-, referring to formulae, shapes and colours at each stage. (The sequence of observations is shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: Yellow tetrahedral [CuCl4]2- first forms pale blue octahedral [Cu(H2O)6]2+ (water replaces chloride); then ammonia acts as a base to give pale blue Cu(OH)2(H2O)4 precipitate; in excess ammonia ligand exchange gives deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+.
steps: Start: [CuCl4]2- is a yellow, tetrahedral complex with four large Cl- ligands.

Pale blue solution: the dilute ammonia solution contains water, which replaces chloride (ligand exchange): [CuCl4]2- + 6H2O -> [Cu(H2O)6]2+ + 4Cl-; the complex becomes octahedral with a coordination number of 6 and is pale blue.
Pale blue precipitate: NH3 acts as a base and removes H+ from coordinated water (deprotonation): [Cu(H2O)6]2+ + 2NH3 -> Cu(OH)2(H2O)4 + 2NH4+, an uncharged octahedral complex.
Deep blue solution: excess NH3 replaces water ligands (ligand exchange): Cu(OH)2(H2O)4 + 4NH3 -> [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ + 2OH- + 2H2O.
[Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ is octahedral (four NH3 and two H2O) and deep blue because the ammonia ligands split the d orbitals by a different amount, so a different colour of light is absorbed.
